deals.headline: IDG Capital pays EUR 100m for 20% of OL Groupe
deals.investor: IDG Capital Partners (IDG European Sports Investment Ltd)
deals.summary: Chinese fund IDG Capital Partners took a 20% stake in Olympique Lyonnais Groupe for EUR 100m and set up a sports-services joint venture with the club; the deal was formalised at a ceremony in Beijing in December 2016. IDG Capital still held 19.74% in July 2022 and sold to Eagle Football in December 2022.

deals.headline: Eagle Football takes 77.49% of OL Groupe for EUR 413.4m
deals.investor: Eagle Football Holdings (John Textor), backed by Iconic Sport Eagle Investment LLC and Elmwood Eagle LLC
deals.seller: Holnest (Jean-Michel Aulas), IDG Capital, Pathé (with OJEJ and SOJER)
deals.source_name: Eagle Football offer document (note d'information, AMF visa, 2023)
deals.summary: Eagle Football bought 39.2m shares at EUR 3.00 and 789,824 OSRANE bonds from Holnest, IDG Capital and Pathé and subscribed a reserved EUR 86m capital increase (28.67m new shares at EUR 3.00), ending with 77.49% of the capital; the block purchase and capital increase totalled EUR 413,357,304. A mandatory tender offer at EUR 3.00 followed in 2023.

deals.evidence: Eagle a émis des obligations (notes) souscrites par Ares, Monroe et CLNI pour un montant maximal en principal de 425.000.000 dollars US, avec une maturité de 6 ans.
deals.headline: Ares, Monroe and Natixis's CLNI fund Eagle's Lyon takeover with up to USD 425m of notes
deals.investor: Ares Sports Media and Entertainment Finance (Ares), Monroe Capital Private Credit Master Fund IV, CL Note Investment LLC (Natixis)
deals.source_name: Eagle Football offer document (note d'information, AMF visa, 2023)
deals.summary: Eagle financed the OL Groupe purchase partly with six-year notes of up to USD 425m in principal subscribed by Ares, Monroe Capital and CLNI, who also took equity warrants in Eagle Holdings; the debt was secured on the OL Groupe shares Eagle acquired. Ares later drove John Textor's removal from Eagle Football Holdings' board (January 2026) and appointed administrators (Cork Gully) to Eagle Bidco in March 2026.

deals.summary: Eagle Football Group sold the women's team, now OL Lyonnes, to Michele Kang in February 2024; it is managed separately from the men's club. The stake and price are not stated on this page.

deals.headline: Eagle Bidco lends EUR 87.3m to EFG during the DNCG appeal
deals.investor: Eagle Football Holdings Bidco (then controlling shareholder)
deals.summary: During the DNCG appeal that kept OL in Ligue 1 for 2025/26, Eagle Football Holdings Bidco lent the company EUR 87.3m in principal, and Michele Kang's YMK Holdings gave OL SASU a EUR 30m bank guarantee. Debts owed to Eagle/Textor entities (EUR 232.6m on a consolidated basis) were released when Kang bought control in June 2026.

deals.headline: Michele Kang buys 87.78% of Eagle Football Group (OL) for USD 30m
deals.investor: Michele Kang (Olympe Bidco SAS / YMK Holdings LLC)
deals.seller: Eagle Football Holdings Bidco Limited (in administration; administrators Cork Gully)
deals.source_name: Eagle Football Group press release of 26 June 2026 (reproduced by ABC Bourse/Actusnews)
deals.summary: After a competitive sale run by Eagle Bidco's administrators, Olympe Bidco bought 154,382,133 EFG shares (87.78% of the capital) for USD 30m (about USD 0.1943 per share; EUR 26.451m), paid partly by offsetting debt YMK Holdings held on Eagle Bidco, which had bought out certain Eagle Bidco lenders. A mandatory tender offer at the same price is to follow, with no squeeze-out planned for 12 months; the group will be renamed Olympique Lyonnais Groupe SA.

deals.headline: Kang commits up to EUR 71m of shareholder loans; OL's senior debt rescheduled
deals.investor: Olympe Bidco (Michele Kang); senior RCF/TL and FCT lenders of OL SASU
deals.source_name: Eagle Football Group press release of 26 June 2026 (reproduced by ABC Bourse/Actusnews)
deals.summary: Olympe Bidco committed up to EUR 71m of subordinated shareholder loans over 2026/27 and 2027/28, with a first EUR 31m tranche at closing and the EUR 40m balance backed by a standby letter of credit (JP Morgan) for OL SASU. OL SASU's RCF/term loan and FCT securitisation lenders agreed to capitalise interest and principal for 18 months and reset covenants, and may name board observers for 24 months.

name: Olympique Lyonnais
notes: OL is held through the listed Eagle Football Group SA (Euronext Paris, ISIN FR0010428771); a move to Euronext Growth and the return to the name Olympique Lyonnais Groupe go to the AGM of 16 October 2026. Revenue is the latest stated figure: FY 2025/26 revenue excluding player trading of EUR 144.0m (unaudited, published 28 July 2026); total revenue including EUR 79.2m of player trading was EUR 223.3m (FY 2024/25: EUR 162.6m and EUR 273.7m). Wages, operating result, pre-tax result and net debt are from the audited FY 2024/25 group accounts (FY 2025/26 results not yet published); the DNCG's 2024/25 accounts for OL SASU alone show EUR 159.0m non-transfer earnings, EUR 155.1m payroll and a EUR 208.6m net loss. H1 2025/26 (to 31 Dec 2025): EBITDA EUR -2.2m, net loss EUR 186.5m after EUR 126.2m of write-downs on Eagle Bidco and Botafogo receivables; financial debts EUR 616.3m. No valuation is recorded: Lyon is outside Football Benchmark's 2026 top 32 and no page states a valuation for the June 2026 deal (Sportune lists its cost as EUR 26.3m). Ares (lender to Eagle) was advised by Macfarlanes on the Kang takeover; Inside World Football reported Ares lent Textor over EUR 400m. The front-of-shirt sponsor for 2026/27 was not confirmed on a citable page (Winamax is on the upper back and XTB on the lower back from 2026/27). John Textor has brought proceedings against the company before the Lyon commercial court (EFG release of 30 July 2026, 'Assignation par John Textor devant le TC de Lyon'). Social followers are the CIES Football Observatory's cumulative count across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and X (published 27 May 2026, via Sportune), not per platform. No attendance figure with a date was found.

ownership_summary: Olympique Lyonnais SASU belongs to Eagle Football Group SA (ex-OL Groupe), listed on Euronext Paris. Since 26 June 2026 Michele Kang controls it through Olympe Bidco SAS (wholly owned by her YMK Holdings LLC), which bought Eagle Football Holdings Bidco's 87.78% (91.46% of votes) out of English administration for USD 30m; a mandatory tender offer for the rest is due by October 2026. Jean-Michel Aulas's holding Holnest keeps 2.41% (5.03% of votes), the free float is 2.91% and treasury shares 6.90%.
